card.name: Reverse drug-interaction statements: no effect
card.fires_on: Words like 'not', 'to', 'no effect' right after a drug name in a sentence saying the second drug does not change the first drug's pharmacokinetics. It marks the turn to the reverse direction of an interaction.

modes.label: Negation after drug
modes.description: 'not' or 'no' after 'does', 'did' or 'had' when a drug is said not to alter another drug's levels.
modes.example: Diazepam does<< not>> alter the pharmacokinetics of propr

modes.label: Hedged no-effect phrasing
modes.description: 'to' or 'effect' inside phrases like 'did not appear to affect' or 'not anticipated to affect'.
modes.example: These immunosuppressants are not anticipated<< to>> affect exposure of EFV.

card.plain: It spots the point where a label says the second drug leaves the first drug's levels unchanged.
